title.text: Creator Campaign Copilot: brief to readout

n1.text:
Brief

- The brand kit prefills every field it can, so a new campaign starts mostly done.
- Starter DMs sit beside the form: the starter each creator will get, written from their past DMs. Creators edit it in their own words.
- Each creator gets one code that is both their comment keyword and their checkout code; the DM link carries it.
- Budget and the paid social CAC benchmark live here because the roster and readout both judge against them.

n2.text:
Roster

- Default sort is past CAC, cheapest first, because that is the rebooking metric.
- New creators show a 'new' tag instead of blank cells, so missing history reads as unknown, not bad.
- A warning about one creator sits under that creator's row; a warning about the whole pick list sits in the budget bar.
- No status or post dates: no one is invited yet. Those start on Creator status.

n3.text:
Drafts and checks

- Flow: starter drafted from past DMs, creator edits or accepts, checks re-run, brand approves.
- Each card shows the creator's stage, how many past DMs set the voice, and how much of the starter they changed.
- Failed checks block Approve and say why, with the offending phrase in the creator's edit highlighted.
- Exact rules (disclosure, link, keyword, length) run in code; the model only judges paraphrased claims.

n4.text:
Creator status

- Status is a pipeline per creator: invited, accepted, connected, ready.
- Anyone not ready 3 days before their post date is flagged first, with a drafted nudge ready to send.
- A declined creator offers a backup swap right in the row, filtered to similar niche and fee.

n5.text:
Readout

- Goal: in a minute, see whether creators beat paid social and where each creator goes next.
- The scatter is the story: fee across, customers up, and the $65 CAC line. Above the line beats ads. The outlier needs no sentence. Hover shows creator, CAC, and one line.
- Each creator lands in one pool, by an exact rule printed on the page. The outlined cell is the metric that placed them.
- Saving a pool feeds Creators, so the next roster starts from proven groups.
- Table and Funnel views with filters sit below, for checking.

n0.text:
Navigation

- App level: Campaigns, Creators, Brand kit. Creators and the brand kit are shared across campaigns.
- Campaign level: breadcrumb, campaign name, and a campaign switcher, with the five steps as a stepper under the name. The steps belong to this campaign, not to the app.
